record.field: Client legal name, group name, and reporting entity are correctly identified.
Financial reporting period and reporting date agree with the financial statements.
Applicable financial reporting framework and applicable auditing standards are identified.
The FAM has a clear purpose, scope, preparation date, and version/revision history.
Preparer, reviewer, engagement partner, and approval dates are documented.
The memorandum is cross-referenced to the relevant audit file, lead schedules, and supporting working papers.
The FAM is consistent with the final financial statements, audit report, and other completion documents.
Outstanding review notes and subsequent revisions are tracked and resolved.
Acceptance or continuance procedures and any significant engagement risks are documented.
Auditor independence and compliance with relevant ethical requirements are confirmed.
Identified independence threats and safeguards or other actions are documented and evaluated.
Engagement terms, management responsibilities, and the agreed reporting framework are appropriately documented.
Any concerns regarding management integrity, competence, or cooperation have been evaluated.
Required consultations, disagreements, and their resolution are documented.
Engagement quality review (EQR), if required, is completed before the auditor's report is dated; required matters are resolved.
The FAM explains the final audit scope, significant changes to the original plan, and reasons for those changes.
All significant assessed risks have a documented audit response and a conclusion supported by evidence.
The team has assessed whether sufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained.
Uncompleted procedures, scope limitations, unavailable evidence, and their implications are resolved or evaluated.
Results from interim work have been rolled forward to year-end and relevant changes addressed.
Audit work performed by specialists, component auditors, or other auditors has been appropriately evaluated.
Audit evidence from contradictory sources, unexpected results, and inconsistent explanations has been investigated.
Significant matters arising after planning and their impact on the audit strategy are documented.
The FAM provides an overall conclusion on whether the audit objectives have been achieved.
Final overall materiality is documented, including the benchmark, percentage, rationale, and calculations.
Performance materiality and its rationale are documented.
Specific materiality and specific performance materiality, where applicable, are documented.
The clearly trivial threshold is documented and distinguished from overall materiality.
Changes in materiality from planning to completion are explained and their consequences evaluated.
All identified misstatements, except those that are clearly trivial, have been accumulated as required.
Corrected misstatements and their effects on the financial statements are documented.
Uncorrected misstatements are listed individually and in aggregate, including tax and related effects where relevant.
Uncorrected misstatements are evaluated for materiality, individually and in aggregate, including qualitative factors.
Management's reasons for not correcting misstatements and the auditor's evaluation are documented.
The required written representation regarding uncorrected misstatements is obtained, where applicable.
The final misstatement summary agrees with the proposed adjustments, passed adjustments, and final trial balance.
Final financial-statement-level and assertion-level risk assessments are documented.
Significant risks identified during the audit and the rationale for classification are addressed.
The presumed fraud risk in revenue recognition has been assessed; any rebuttal is justified and documented as required.
Management override procedures, including journal entry testing, are completed and concluded upon.
Significant accounting estimates and unusual or complex transactions have been assessed for possible management bias.
Fraud inquiries, team discussions, identified fraud indicators, and responses are documented.
Actual or suspected fraud and non-compliance with laws and regulations have been evaluated, including required communications.
Related-party transactions and significant transactions outside the normal course of business have been addressed.
The final FAM explains whether audit results changed the initial risk assessment or required additional procedures.
The final control strategy, including reliance or non-reliance on controls, is documented.
Control testing results and deviations are summarized, including implications for substantive testing.
Significant control deficiencies and other reportable deficiencies are evaluated and classified appropriately.
Required written communications of significant deficiencies have been issued to the appropriate parties.
IT general controls and relevant automated controls are addressed where relied upon or otherwise relevant.
IT control deficiencies, system changes, access issues, interfaces, and data reliability issues are evaluated.
The FAM makes clear that an ordinary financial statement audit does not, by itself, express an opinion on internal control effectiveness.
Control findings, recommendations, management responses, and communication references are consistent.
Cash, bank balances, bank reconciliations, restrictions, and confirmations are concluded upon.
Revenue, including occurrence, accuracy, cut-off, presentation, and applicable disclosures, is concluded upon.
Trade and other receivables, confirmations, subsequent receipts, impairment/ECL, and aging are concluded upon.
Inventory existence, count results, costing, net realizable value, obsolescence, and cut-off are concluded upon.
PPE, additions, disposals, depreciation, impairment indicators, and capitalization are concluded upon.
Accounts payable, accruals, provisions, and search for unrecorded liabilities are concluded upon.
Borrowings, interest, covenant compliance, current/non-current classification, and security are concluded upon.
Payroll, employee benefits, pensions, and related estimates are concluded upon where material or relevant.
Current tax, deferred tax, uncertain tax positions, and tax exposures are concluded upon.
Investments, financial instruments, fair value measurements, and impairment are concluded upon where applicable.
Leases, contract assets/liabilities, and other significant or industry-specific accounts are concluded upon where applicable.
Equity, reserves, dividends, non-controlling interests, and movements in capital are concluded upon.
Provisions, contingencies, litigation, guarantees, commitments, and legal exposures are concluded upon.
Related-party balances, transactions, disclosures, and completeness of related-party identification are concluded upon.
All material financial statement line items and disclosures have a documented conclusion or a clear reference to supporting workpapers.
Accounting policies, estimates, judgments, classification, presentation, and disclosures comply with the applicable framework.
Significant accounting estimates and related disclosures are identified and evaluated.
Methods, assumptions, data, estimation uncertainty, and management bias have been assessed.
Relevant sensitivity analyses, retrospective reviews, and contradictory evidence are considered where appropriate.
The work of management's experts has been evaluated where used as audit evidence.
Auditor's experts, if used, have appropriate competence, capabilities, and objectivity; scope and results are documented.
Significant valuation, actuarial, impairment, ECL, and fair value conclusions are cross-referenced to detailed workpapers.
Management's going-concern assessment has been obtained and evaluated.
The assessment period, forecasts, assumptions, financing plans, and debt maturities have been evaluated.
Cash-flow forecasts and sensitivity analyses have been challenged where risks or uncertainties warrant.
Covenants, refinancing, liquidity shortfalls, customer/supplier dependency, and other warning indicators are evaluated.
Events or conditions that may cast significant doubt on going concern and management's mitigating plans are documented.
The auditor's conclusion on the appropriateness of the going-concern basis and any material uncertainty is documented.
Financial statement disclosures and implications for the auditor's report are evaluated and consistent with the conclusion.
Subsequent-event procedures cover the period through the auditor's report date, as required.
Relevant board minutes, management inquiries, interim financial information, and legal updates are considered.
Events requiring adjustment or disclosure are identified, evaluated, and reflected appropriately.
The auditor's responsibilities for other information, where applicable, have been completed and concluded upon.
Known facts discovered after the auditor's report date, if any, have been addressed under the applicable requirements.
Relevant laws and regulations with a direct effect on material financial statement amounts or disclosures are addressed.
Inquiries and procedures regarding other laws and regulations have been performed as required.
Known or suspected non-compliance, regulatory investigations, and related consequences are evaluated.
Legal letters, litigation schedules, tax correspondence, and regulatory communications are evaluated where relevant.
Required reporting or communications to management, TCWG, regulators, or other parties are documented.
The group scope and identification of components are documented where a group audit applies.
Component materiality, scope, significant risks, and instructions are addressed as required.
The group engagement team has evaluated component auditor competence, independence, and involvement as required.
Significant component findings, misstatements, and control matters are evaluated and resolved.
Consolidation entries, intercompany eliminations, uniform accounting policies, and group disclosures are concluded upon.
The group auditor's final conclusion is supported by sufficient appropriate evidence across the group.
Written representations are dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the auditor's report date and cover the required period.
Representations address management's responsibilities and all matters required by the applicable standards.
Representations are consistent with other audit evidence; inconsistencies are investigated.
Refusals, limitations, or doubts about the reliability of representations are evaluated for their effect on the audit opinion.
Significant delays, withheld information, restrictions, or other difficulties caused by management are documented.
Required communications about the audit's scope and timing and significant risks are documented.
Significant findings, significant qualitative accounting matters, and major judgments are communicated as required.
Required communications concerning auditor independence are completed.
Significant deficiencies in internal control are communicated in writing as required.
Corrected and uncorrected misstatements and their effects are communicated as required.
Significant difficulties, disagreements with management, and unresolved matters are documented and communicated as required.
Communications concerning fraud, non-compliance, related parties, going concern, and reporting matters are completed where required.
Copies of written communications and records of oral communications, including dates and recipients, are retained.
The proposed audit opinion is supported by the overall audit conclusions and evidence obtained.
The financial statements are assessed for compliance with the applicable reporting framework, including presentation and disclosures.
Any modified opinion, basis for modification, or scope limitation is evaluated and documented.
Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraphs are considered where relevant and justified.
Key Audit Matters (KAM) are determined and reported when SA 701 applies; any applicable exception is documented.
Going-concern reporting, including material uncertainty reporting where applicable, is consistent with the audit conclusion.
The auditor's report date, addressee, entity identification, financial statements covered, and prescribed wording are verified.
Other reporting responsibilities required by laws, regulations, or engagement terms are considered.
The final auditor's report agrees with the final approved financial statements and relevant completion documentation.
Final analytical procedures have been performed to assist the overall conclusion on whether the financial statements are consistent with the auditor's understanding.
Unexpected relationships, significant variances, and unexplained fluctuations have been investigated.
Final financial results are compared with prior year, budget/forecast, and relevant expectations where appropriate.
The aggregate effect of corrected and uncorrected misstatements is evaluated.
Audit evidence from different areas is considered collectively, including whether it contradicts management's assertions.
The FAM concludes whether the financial statements as a whole are materially misstated.
All significant audit matters and review notes are resolved or appropriately documented before report release.
The FAM is consistent with the final trial balance, lead schedules, adjustment summary, and disclosure checklist.
The audit file includes documentation sufficient for an experienced auditor to understand the work performed, evidence obtained, and conclusions reached.
The final audit documentation is assembled within the applicable deadline and subsequent changes are documented.
Required engagement partner review and engagement quality review, if applicable, are completed and documented.
The FAM includes a clear overall conclusion and appropriate preparer, reviewer, and partner sign-off.
Retention, confidentiality, access controls, and archiving comply with firm policy and applicable requirements.
